text:
aria: Heads-up from today's onboarding: the sample notebook shows `async with client` + `async for` for streaming and it's tripping people. When an interrupt (kernel stop / SIGINT) occurs the final chunk can be repeated and the outgoing TCP stays ESTABLISHED until process exit.

tom: ouch. can you paste the tiny repro you used?

aria: minimal repro (uses stream_chat SSE-like behavior):
```py
async def demo():
    async with RedwoodClient(token=...) as client:
        async for e in client.stream_chat(model=\"sage-7B\", messages=[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hi\"}]):
            print(e.text)

asyncio.run(demo())
```
interrupt the cell after a few messages. sometimes last message prints twice. `ss` shows tcp to api still ESTABLISHED.

lee: which python/aiohttp/sdk versions? any custom telemetry?

aria: redwood-py 0.8.3, python 3.11.4, aiohttp 3.9.5. no telemetry. also repros in a tiny FastAPI background task when the endpoint cancels the runner.

tom: sounds like a race between the reader task flushing the final buffer and the generator finalizer running on cancel. the SDK might be both putting the final event on an internal queue and then also re-emitting it while unwinding.

lee: two immediate experiments: 1) call `it = client.stream_chat().__aiter__()` then `await it.aclose()` in finally — does that always close the socket? 2) run a local test server that emits a final event then pauses so we can trigger cancel in the client.

aria: 1) explicit `await it.aclose()` in finally closes socket reliably and prevents the duplicate. 2) repro'd with a small aiohttp test server: duplicate only appears when we cancel (Ctrl-C / kernel interrupt).

tom: ok. proposal: make `aclose()` idempotent and no-op if already closed; centralize final emit so only one path writes last event. also export a StreamIterator alias in `typing` so users can do `it: StreamIterator[StreamEvent] = client.stream_chat().__aiter__()` without hacks.

lee: agree. another ergonomic issue: mypy complains when people assign `it = client.stream_chat().__aiter__()` because `__aiter__()` is typed as `AsyncIterator[Any]` by default. we should provide narrow generics on the returned iterator type in the stubs.

aria: for onboarding notebook we'll add a short note under the streaming section: "In interactive environments, keyboard interrupts may trigger generator finalizers; prefer explicit iterator close in a finally block during demos." and a one-line snippet. that will avoid the demo embarrassment.

tom: implementation note: instead of making __aexit__ await aclose (which can re-enter cancellation), we can schedule aclose with loop.call_soon and return immediately; but as ion pointed out in a different thread that trades determinism for safety. I'd prefer to make aclose robust and idempotent so callers can safely await in finally.

lee: test idea: add a pytest-asyncio test that spins up a fake SSE server, starts client stream, consumes a few events, then cancels the consuming task and asserts: (a) socket closed, (b) last event delivered at most once, (c) no unhandled CancelledError.

aria: i'll attach the notebook patch and the small aiohttp repro to the issue. ci-bot: can you open an issue for tracking?

ci-bot: Created issue #4602 in redwood-python: "streaming: duplicate final chunk + socket leak on interrupt; typing ergonomics for async iterators" (https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python/issues/4602) :white_check_mark:

tom: i'll pick the stub/typing fix (export StreamIterator[T], narrow __aiter__ return types). lee can implement idempotent aclose and centralize final emit. aria will add the notebook note and attach repro.

lee: follow-up: we should also audit the JS/TS SDK for similar finalization idempotency — might be a cross-sdk pattern.

aria: thanks folks, saved a few awkward demo moments today. :coffee:
